summary: Gerlach Royen was a linguist who earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck. After teaching at Gymnasium Immaculatae Conceptionis (1905–1911), he served as extraordinary professor of comparative and general linguistics at Utrecht University (1932–1943).
Gernot Böhme worked in the field of philosophy. He studied at the University of Hamburg from around 1961 to 1965 and held a post at the Technical University of Darmstadt from circa 1977 to 2002.

Gernot Rotter studied at the University of Tübingen and at the University of Bonn (~1964–1967) under Annemarie Schimmel. He later held an academic appointment at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1984 to 2005.

Gernot Schmidt was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at the Free University of Berlin under Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle, habilitated at the University of Bonn, and became professor of IE linguistics there in 1980.

Gerrit Jan Held worked in Indology and anthropology. He earned his Ph.D. at Leiden University under J. P. B. de Josselin de Jong, later serving as professor of cultural anthropology at the University of Indonesia and visiting professor at Yale.

Gerrit Jan Meulenbeld was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University (~1946–1954) under Jan Gonda. He later served as associate professor of Indology at the University of Groningen from 1978 to 1986.

Gert Klingenschmitt specialized in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his PhD under Karl Hoffmann and his Habilitation at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg, later holding the chair for Indo-European linguistics at the University of Regensburg (1983–2006).

Geshe Gendun Lodro was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Drepung Gomang Dratsang under Khensur Ngawang Legden, he held faculty posts at Drepung Gomang, Hamburg University, and the University of Virginia.

Geshe Jampa Tegchok was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who studied at Sera Monastery. He served as abbot and resident teacher at Nalanda Monastery (~1982–1993) and resident teacher at Land of Medicine Buddha (~1998–2001).
Geshe Karma Sonam is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts attested at Gyume Tantric College in 1987 and at Sera Monastery in 1992.

Geshe Lhakdor specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the Central School for Tibetans, Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, University of Delhi, and Drepung Loseling Monastery, later serving at Tibet House, New Delhi, and as director of LTWA.

Geshe Lhundup Sopa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Gaden Chokhor and Sera Jey monasteries under several teachers, he served as a professor of Buddhist studies at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from 1967 onward.

Geshe Lobsang Tharchin was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his studies at Sera Monastery, earning his Lharampa Geshe degree by 1953, and also studied at Gyume Tantric College.

Geshe Losang Chödar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. In 2010, he was attested holding posts at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and as a Tibetan editor at the Institute of Tibetan Classics.
Geshe Ngawang Nyima was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held appointments at Leiden University and served as abbot and Geshe of sGo-mang sgrva-tshang at Drepung Monastery.

Geshe Ngawang Samten specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at CIHTS and Ganden Shartse Monastery, he served as chief editor at CIHTS and held visiting positions at Hampshire, Amherst, Smith, and the University of Tasmania.
Geshe Palden Dragpa is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He held a post as librarian at Tibet House in New Delhi, attested between 1987 and 2004.

Geshe Palden Drakpa is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987 and served as librarian at Tibet House, New Delhi, attested in 1988.

Geshe Rabten was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Geshe Lharampa degree at Sera Monastery studying under Trijang Rinpoche, and later taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1964–1969).

Geshe Sonam Rinchen specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and became a resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives in 1978.
